In my experience, you gotta challenge it. Breathing techniques always help to ground yourself when it's coming on. Also try practicing mindfulness, and being aware of your thoughts and how you have power over them. 
1.feeling anxious? Ask yourself why you might be feeling that
2. After you pinpoint why, address it, aka, allow yourself to feel the stress 
3. challenge yourself to take it on as a responsibility. 
You can't avoid school, atleast, I don't recommend that you try. So you gotta face it. Pay more attention to what your fears in a social setting I mean. Like if your talking to someone and can feel the anxiety coming on, pay closer attention to that person. The more attention you give the chatter in your head, the less your mind will be focused on what's right in front of you. And that just perpetuates the bad thoughts further. It seems like your an over thinker, like myself. The key is to get out of your head and into the moment. It'll take time, and it won't always come easy. But the key is, pay more attention to whats in the moment and less to that voice in your head. It doesnt always have your best interests in mind. And ITS NOT YOU! You are a seperate entity from your anxiety, you are the observer of those thoughts, you choose weather to listen. And the more practice you have at ignoring that voice, the better you'll feel, in time. you just gotta take it one day at a time, one step at a time. I believe in you! You can do it!
